features.text: The patient experiences sharp, shooting, and hot pain on the right side of the face, especially around the cheekbone.
The pain has been present for a couple of months.
The patient has not experienced numbness or tingling on the affected side.
The patient has no dental issues or recent dental procedures on the affected side.
The patient has no history of facial trauma.
The patient has not had any recent sinus infections.
The patient has not experienced any issues with vision, such as blurriness or double vision.
The pain is triggered by cold temperatures, touching the area, or certain sensory input.
The pain episodes typically last a few minutes, sometimes up to an hour.
The patient has not experienced numbness, tingling, or weakness on the same side of the face during episodes.
The pain is not triggered by chewing, speaking, or brushing teeth.
The pain is localized to the right cheekbone area and does not radiate to the eye, jaw, or neck.
The patient has no history of herpes zoster or other neurological conditions.
The patient has not experienced changes in vision, eye redness, tearing, or nasal congestion associated with the pain.
The pain is not triggered by opening the mouth wide or moving the jaw.
The patient has no issues with teeth or gums.
The pain is not related to specific foods or activities.
The patient has not noticed any patterns in when the episodes occur, such as more frequently during certain times of the day or in response to specific environmental factors.
